newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar raises interest rate on riyal deposits.
newsitem.headline: Qatar raises interest rate on riyal deposits.

text.p: Qatar's Central Bank on Sunday raised the interest rate on riyal deposits by 0.25 percentage points to 6.75 percent, bankers said.

"The measure is intended to ensure better yield to depositors and stem the outflow of local funds into the dollar or other foreign currencies," said Mohamed Atiq, acting general manager of Doha Bank Ltd, the country's second largest bank.
"The QCB decision is also in line with the similar increase in dollar rates announced by the U.S. Federal Reserve 10 days earlier," he told Reuters.
Qatar's riyal is pegged to the dollar for all international transactions.

Last year, the Central Bank freed interest rates on loans and advances after 25 years of control and left it to market forces to determine. But it kept control on deposit rates, which it revises in line with changes in dollar rates.
